fields.title: Weekly Observation October 17 — NVIDIA's Throne, Solid
fields.summary: With NVIDIA holding the Sun's position at $5.17 trillion, surges in retail, pharmaceuticals, and payments, combined with semiconductor weakness, are reshaping the order of the universe.
fields.body:
The Sun's Sustained Position

During this week's observation period, NVIDIA maintained the Sun's throne with a market cap of $5.17 trillion. The throne saw no change from last week, and the gap with Apple ($5.01 trillion) has narrowed to $0.16 trillion. The order of the top 5 planets remains largely stable: Alphabet ($4.12 trillion), Microsoft ($3.93 trillion), and Amazon ($2.7 trillion).

Giant planets in the technology sector continue to occupy the center of the universe, yet weekly volatility shows an increasing trend. This is interpreted as a signal suggesting system rebalancing from a cosmic perspective.

Shifting Visible Light

What stands out in weekly surging sectors is the activity of fields other than technology. Walmart (+6.7%) revealed the resilience of the retail sector, while Eli Lilly (+6.6%) demonstrated structural strength in the pharmaceutical industry. Visa's (+4.5%) rise shows the elasticity of the global payment ecosystem.

In contrast, contraction in the semiconductor sector is notable. Samsung Electronics' (-18.0%) sharp decline marks the largest drop in the universe this week, while Micron Technology (-14.4%) and AMD (-13.0%) also showed weakness in the same category. This suggests an adjustment away from technology-centric focus is underway.

Universe's Entry and Exit

During this observation period, Exxon Mobil was included in top-tier entry observations, while SK Hynix was removed from the top ranks. Partial reassessment of the energy sector and restructuring of the semiconductor sector are proceeding simultaneously.

Potential observation targets like SanDisk (momentum 801), MediaTek (202), and Dell (199) are showing elevated momentum. The future trajectory of these planets appears closely linked to structural changes in the semiconductor industry as a whole.

Observer's Record

As of October 17, 2026, the order of the universe stands at the boundary between solidity and change. The Sun's position has not wavered, yet the orbital paths of surrounding planets are visibly shifting. According to records, this may signal more distinct restructuring to come in the following week.
